name: Sidebar Navigation
description: An app's side navigation: groups of links with optional nested lists, a collapsible icon rail whose links keep their names, a saved collapsed state applied before the first paint, and the same nav as a drawer below 1024 px, with the rest of the page inert while it's open.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The docked sidebar is page content; the drawer is a modal; tooltips are popovers.

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend an app's side navigation: groups of links, optional nested lists, an optional collapsed icon rail, and a drawer below 1024 px. In the rail, labels are hidden visually only, so every link keeps its name. A saved collapsed state is applied before the first paint, so the sidebar never jumps. Below 1024 px the same nav is a drawer, and the rest of the page is inert while it's open. Build on the project's navigation or sidebar component when it has a suitable one. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A labelled <nav> with links in lists, aria-current="page" on the current one, and groups and nested lists behind disclosure buttons whose closed lists are hidden
A 64 px icon rail (an 80 px rail with labels is an option) whose links keep their names, with tooltips that meet WCAG 1.4.13 and badges as dots
An item with children in the rail expands the sidebar and opens its group
The collapsed state saved under the app's own prefix, or in a cookie, and applied before the first paint
Optional search whose number of matches is announced politely
Below 1024 px, the same nav as a drawer with a Close button, with the rest of the page inert while it's open
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the router, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has a sidebar or navigation component, configure or extend it to meet this guide instead of building another one, and keep its API.
2. Choose what the task needs: groups, nested lists, the rail, saving its state, badges, search, hover expand. Leave out the rest.
3. Build the nav, its lists, and the disclosure buttons for groups (componentSpec.anatomy).
4. For the rail, hide labels visually only (frameworkPatterns.collapsedLabels), add the toggle, and save its state before the first paint (frameworkPatterns.savedState).
5. Below 1024 px, make the same nav a drawer (implementationDetails.drawer).
6. Add search and badges if the task needs them (implementationDetails.search, componentSpec.anatomy.slotNotes.badge).
7. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, and 200% zoom, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

componentSpec.goal: Give an app one place for its main sections, which takes little room when collapsed, keeps every link named and reachable, and works the same with a keyboard, a pointer, a touch screen, and a screen reader.

anatomy.hierarchy: nav "Main" → optional header and search | groups: label and list of items (icon, label, badge), an item with children followed by its nested list | optional footer | collapse toggle; below 1024 px the same nav is a drawer with a Close button over a backdrop

slotNotes.nav: The sidebar is a <nav> labelled for its purpose ("Main"). An <aside> can't take role="navigation", so the root is the <nav> itself.
slotNotes.lists: Links sit in lists (<ul>), in groups under visible group labels; a nested list sits inside its parent's <li>. The DOM order is the order on screen, top to bottom, and so is the Tab order.
slotNotes.currentLink: The current page's link has aria-current="page", marked by more than color: a bar at its edge with 3:1 contrast (WCAG 1.4.11), or a stronger background.
slotNotes.groupButton: An item with children is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls that shows its nested list; focus stays on it, and several groups can be open. A closed list is hidden (hidden, or display: none once a closing animation ends), so its links aren't in the Tab order; a list animated to height 0 alone keeps them there. An item with its own page and children needs two controls: the link, and a separate button for the list.
slotNotes.badge: A badge's count is part of the link's text ("Orders 12 new"), visually hidden where the badge shows only "99+" or a dot. A plain <span> can't take an aria-label.
slotNotes.unavailableLink: Leave out items the person can't use. One that has to show as unavailable for now is an <a> without href, with role="link", tabindex="0", and aria-disabled="true", so it's still found and does nothing; say why next to it. A link that opens a new tab says so.
slotNotes.collapseToggle: The collapse toggle is a button whose name says what it does: "Collapse sidebar", then "Expand sidebar". Don't add aria-expanded to a name that changes, or it reads as a double state ("Collapse sidebar, expanded"); a stable name with aria-expanded is the other way. Focus stays on the toggle.
slotNotes.tooltip: Tooltips show the label on hover and on focus. They don't add aria-describedby: the name already has the label, so it would be read twice. They meet WCAG 1.4.13: Escape closes them, the pointer can move onto them, and they stay while the pointer or focus is on the link or the tooltip. Draw them in the top layer (the popover attribute), so the scrolling column doesn't clip them.

collapsed.description: Whether the docked sidebar is the icon rail; from 1024 px only.
collapsed.persistence: Optional: a cookie the server reads, or storage under the app's own prefix applied by an inline script before the first paint

drawerOpen.description: Whether the drawer is open, below 1024 px.

expandedGroups.description: The groups whose nested lists show; the current page's group is always among them on load.

activeItem.description: The link for the current page, which gets aria-current="page".

query.description: Optional search text that filters the links.

interactions.accessibilityNotes: Focus stays on the toggle; its name changes between "Collapse sidebar" and "Expand sidebar".
Focus stays on the button; a closed list is hidden.
Focus stays on the item's button.
Close, Escape, a click on the backdrop, and a followed link close it.

A matchMedia change listener. Focus on what hides moves to what stays: from the Menu button or Close to the current page's link (or the first link that shows) when the sidebar docks, from the sidebar to the Menu button when it hides; focus anywhere else stays. Chromium drops focus from a hidden element before the listener runs, so the last focused element tells where it was.

responsiveBehavior.fromDesktop: From 1024 px: docked in its own column, expanded (260 px) or collapsed (64 px), with the collapse toggle.
responsiveBehavior.belowDesktop: Below 1024 px: the drawer (implementationDetails.drawer), closed by default, always expanded when open.
responsiveBehavior.reflow: At 320 px wide the drawer is 85% of the window, and labels wrap.

variants.labelledRail: An 80 px rail with a short label under each icon, instead of the 64 px icon-only rail.
variants.compact: Styling, which the project's design decides: smaller items and icons.
variants.floating: Styling, which the project's design decides: inset from the edge with rounded corners.
variants.hoverExpand: Optional: hover expand. After a short delay (about 300 ms), the rail expands over the content while the pointer is on it, without moving the page, and collapses when the pointer leaves. Keyboard focus doesn't expand it; tooltips show the labels.

navigationGroups.shape: { label, items: { label, href?, icon, badge?: { text, spoken }, external?, unavailable?, children?: Item[] }[] }[]
navigationGroups.notes: An item with children gets a disclosure button; with an href as well, it gets both a link and a button. badge.spoken is the count in words for the link's name ("12 new").

widthChange.notes: overflow-x: hidden on the column and its scrolling area during the change.

animations.reducedMotion: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing slides; the width and the drawer change at once.

requirements.1.3.1: A labelled nav with lists, and group buttons that expose their state.
requirements.1.4.1: The current item is marked by more than color.
requirements.1.4.11: The current item's marker and focus indicators meet 3:1.
requirements.1.4.13: Tooltips can be dismissed with Escape, hovered, and stay while the pointer or focus is there.
requirements.2.1.1: Every link, group, the toggle, and the drawer work from the keyboard.
requirements.2.4.1: A skip link goes past the sidebar when it comes first.
requirements.2.4.3: Focus returns to the Menu button when the drawer closes, and stays on the same link when it docks.
requirements.2.5.8: Items and buttons are at least 24 px tall.
requirements.4.1.2: Every link keeps its name in the rail; group buttons expose aria-expanded.
requirements.4.1.3: The number of search matches is announced through one status region.

keyboardNavigation.tab: Moves through the links and buttons in the order on screen; a closed group's links are skipped.
keyboardNavigation.enterSpace: Follows links, and opens or closes groups.
keyboardNavigation.escape: Closes a tooltip, or the drawer.
keyboardNavigation.arrows: Optional, as one set with Home and End, as in the APG disclosure navigation example; Tab works without them.

searchStatus.note: One region, in the page before it changes

screenReader.rail: Each link reads its label and badge count in the rail as in the expanded sidebar.

focusManagement.drawer: While it's open, everything else on the page is inert (the Modal Dialog guide's model, without a focus-trap library), so focus and screen readers stay in it, and the page behind doesn't scroll. It makes inert only what isn't inert yet, and closing undoes only that, so a part of the page the app made inert stays inert. It shows expanded, whatever the saved state, 260 px wide or 85% of the window on phones.
focusManagement.breakpoint: If the window gets wider than 1024 px while it's open, it docks, the inertness it added goes, and focus on one of its links stays there, since it's the same element. When the window crosses 1024 px, focus on an element that hides moves to the nearest control that stays, and focus anywhere else stays where it is: widening hides the Menu button and Close, so focus on them, the drawer open or closed, moves to the current page's link, or to the first link that shows when that one is in a closed group, and narrowing hides the docked sidebar, so focus in it moves to the Menu button. React to a matchMedia change, not to resize events. Chromium drops focus from an element a media query hides before the listener runs, so remember the last focused element and check whether it still shows. The Dashboard Layout guide's drawer snippet shows this.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version.

savedState.description: The saved collapsed state, applied by an inline script in <head> before the first paint, and the collapse toggle that saves it; storage is read and written in try and catch.
savedState.html:
<!-- In <head>, before the stylesheets render: apply the saved state, so the sidebar doesn't
     jump. "acme" stands for the app's own storage prefix. -->
<script>
  try {
    if (localStorage.getItem('acme.sidebar') === 'collapsed') {
      document.documentElement.dataset.sidebar = 'collapsed';
    }
  } catch {
    // Storage can be blocked; the sidebar then starts expanded
  }
</script>

collapsedLabels.description: Links whose labels and badge counts are hidden visually only in the rail, so screen readers still read them, and a badge shown as a dot.
collapsedLabels.html:
• Orders 12 new
  • Customers

implementationDetails.rail: Suggested sizes: 260 px expanded, and a 64 px icon-only rail collapsed. An 80 px rail with a short label under each icon is an option; it helps people who don't know the icons or can't hover for a tooltip. The rail is for 1024 px and wider, and so is its saved state: scope its styles to that width, as the snippet does. Below it, the sidebar is the drawer, always expanded, and the collapse toggle is hidden. Unscoped, a saved rail shrinks the drawer to 64 px and hides its labels. The collapse toggle is a button whose name says what it does: "Collapse sidebar", then "Expand sidebar". Don't add aria-expanded to a name that changes, or it reads as a double state ("Collapse sidebar, expanded"); a stable name with aria-expanded is the other way. Focus stays on the toggle. Collapsed, the labels are hidden visually only, so every link keeps its name; icons are aria-hidden. A badge shows as a dot on its icon, its number hidden visually the same way. If the dot has a ring to set it off from the icon, the ring takes the sidebar's background color; a white ring shows as a halo in dark mode. Tooltips show the label on hover and on focus. They don't add aria-describedby: the name already has the label, so it would be read twice. They meet WCAG 1.4.13: Escape closes them, the pointer can move onto them, and they stay while the pointer or focus is on the link or the tooltip. Draw them in the top layer (the popover attribute), so the scrolling column doesn't clip them. An item with children, pressed in the rail, expands the sidebar, as the toggle does, and opens its group, with focus kept on it. A search field shows as a search button that does the same and moves focus into the field.
implementationDetails.savedState: Saving the collapsed state is optional. When the product saves it, keep it where the project keeps preferences: a cookie the server reads, so the server renders the right width, or storage under the app's own prefix (acme.sidebar, where acme stands for that prefix), applied by a small inline script in <head> before the first paint. Reading it after hydration and hiding the jump with a fade still makes the sidebar jump on every page load for everyone who keeps it collapsed. Storage can be blocked, so read and write it in try and catch; the sidebar then starts expanded, and the toggle still works on the page. Where the framework renders <html> itself, as a Next.js root layout does, the attribute the script sets differs from the server's HTML, so tell the framework (React's suppressHydrationWarning on <html>).
implementationDetails.search: Optional: a labelled <input type="search"> ("Filter navigation") above the groups filters the links by their labels, opens the groups that have matches, and keeps the field in place when nothing matches. The number of matches goes to one polite status region once typing pauses ("3 links", "No links match"; WCAG 4.1.3).
implementationDetails.drawer: Below 1024 px, the same <nav> becomes a drawer, opened by a Menu button in the header. There's no second copy, so no id appears twice, and open groups and the search stay as they were. While it's open, everything else on the page is inert (the Modal Dialog guide's model, without a focus-trap library), so focus and screen readers stay in it, and the page behind doesn't scroll. It makes inert only what isn't inert yet, and closing undoes only that, so a part of the page the app made inert stays inert. It shows expanded, whatever the saved state, 260 px wide or 85% of the window on phones. It has a visible Close button ("Close menu"), because touch screen readers have no Escape key, and it also closes on Escape, on a click on the backdrop, and when a link in it is followed. Focus returns to the Menu button. Closed, it's display: none; with a closing animation, it's inert from the moment closing starts. If the window gets wider than 1024 px while it's open, it docks, the inertness it added goes, and focus on one of its links stays there, since it's the same element. When the window crosses 1024 px, focus on an element that hides moves to the nearest control that stays, and focus anywhere else stays where it is: widening hides the Menu button and Close, so focus on them, the drawer open or closed, moves to the current page's link, or to the first link that shows when that one is in a closed group, and narrowing hides the docked sidebar, so focus in it moves to the Menu button. React to a matchMedia change, not to resize events. Chromium drops focus from an element a media query hides before the listener runs, so remember the last focused element and check whether it still shows. The Dashboard Layout guide's drawer snippet shows this.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The docked sidebar is page content; the drawer is a modal; tooltips are popovers.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. Items are 40 px tall (44 px is comfortable for touch), icons 20 px, nested lists indented 16 px per level. Keep nesting to two or three levels. Text meets 4.5:1, and the current item's marker and focus indicators 3:1. Check the project's own colors. Labels wrap; nothing is cut off with an ellipsis. Motion is optional: the width changes over 200 ms, and the drawer slides in over 250 ms. During the width change, overflow-x: hidden on the column and on its scrolling area stops a scrollbar from flashing. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing slides.

edgeCases.deepNesting: Past three levels, flatten the tree or move the deeper pages into their section's own navigation.
edgeCases.manyItems: The column scrolls on its own, and the current link scrolls into view.
edgeCases.rightSide: Logical properties (inset-inline-start, margin-inline-start) put the sidebar and the drawer on the start side in right-to-left text, or on either side by choice.
edgeCases.topBar: The sidebar starts below it: its sticky top is the bar's height. The drawer covers both.
edgeCases.noScript: Render the links on the server, with the current group open.

must: Build on the project's sidebar or navigation component when it has a suitable one, and keep its API
Hide labels visually only in the rail, so every link keeps its name
Hide closed nested lists and the closed drawer, so their links are out of the Tab order
Apply a saved collapsed state before the first paint, and only from 1024 px
Use one nav for the docked sidebar and the drawer
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a focus-trap, tooltip, or scroll-lock library, without asking
Put role="navigation" on an aside, or role="menu" on lists of links
Read the saved state after hydration, or store it under a prefix other than the app's own
Remove labels with display: none in the rail, or name links only through a tooltip's aria-describedby
Render a second copy of the sidebar for the drawer
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The sidebar is a nav labelled for its purpose, with its links in lists and aria-current="page" on the current one, marked by more than color
An item with children is a button with aria-expanded that shows its nested list, and a closed list is hidden, so its links are out of the Tab order
The group with the current page opens on load and on route changes, and its link scrolls into view
Collapsed to the rail, every link keeps its name (the label visually hidden, the icon aria-hidden), and a badge's count is in the link's name
Tooltips in the rail show on hover and on focus, close on Escape, can be hovered, and add no aria-describedby
In the rail, an item with children expands the sidebar and opens its group, with focus kept on it
The collapse toggle's name says what it does, focus stays on it, and the choice is saved under the app's own prefix
A saved collapsed state applies before the first paint, so the sidebar doesn't jump on load; with storage blocked it starts expanded
The search field's number of matches is said in one polite status region
Below 1024 px, the same nav opens as a drawer with a visible Close button; while it's open, the rest of the page is inert and doesn't scroll
Close, Escape, the backdrop, and a followed link close the drawer, focus returns to the Menu button, and what was inert before the drawer opened stays inert

Crossing 1024 px either way, focus on what hides moves to what stays: from the Menu button or Close to the current page's link (or the first link that shows, when that one is in a closed group), and from the sidebar to the Menu button; focus anywhere else stays where it is
The rail and its saved state apply from 1024 px only: the drawer is always expanded, without the collapse toggle
Labels wrap instead of being cut off, and under reduced motion nothing slides
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
